original.target_description: German first-year pre-service teachers’ judgments of fictitious ninth graders’ interest, reality-connected versus intra-mathematical problems, adjusted for perceived task difficulty; paired t-test. This is judgments of students’ interest, not teachers’ own interest.

n.exclusions: No exclusions reported in the located method/results; paired-test degrees of freedom agree with the reported participant count.

replication.target_description: Spanish pre-service primary-school teachers’ own task-specific interest across intramathematical, word and modelling problems; omnibus Friedman test. This is an elaboration of the original judgment outcome.

n.location: Results, Table 2 and its introductory paragraph; Methods, Sample and data collection
n.quote: Table 2 shows the average situational interest of 80 pre-service teachers
n.sample_role: pre-service teachers; participants in within-person interest analysis
n.exclusions: Questionnaires discarded if one of two parts was not completed; missing values were 6% of the total sample, not split by population. Blank individual interest items omitted when computing participant means. Results explicitly describe 80 participants in each population.

es.location: Results, Pre-service teachers’ task-specific interest, hypothesis-test paragraph following Table 2; unpaginated cached postprint

p.location: Results, Pre-service teachers’ task-specific interest, hypothesis-test paragraph following Table 2; unpaginated cached postprint

reported_success.location: Conclusions, paragraph on the pre-service-teacher adaptation
reported_success.quote: These results complement those of the original study

notes: Known outcome discrepancy: original pre-service teachers judged students’ interest, whereas replication pre-service teachers reported their own interest after solving problems. Original target_match=false for the supplied own-interest description. Original located statistics are for the explicitly identified judgment test and are not merged with replication values. Authors call this an adaptation/complement; no explicit success/failure verdict for this outcome was established. Replication locator empty; neutral description identifies the omnibus Friedman test unambiguously.
